# Decisions: record-hygiene-quotes

- 2026-08-04T09:26:00.789Z — chose **A quote-aware character scan (shellSegments) that splits only on separators appearing outside quotes, and returns "cannot scan" — resolved toward logging — for unbalanced quotes and for command substitution ($( or backtick outside single quotes). It also treats a lone & as a separator unless it belongs to a >&/<& redirect.** over Keeping the quote-unaware regex split that SPEC lines 779-781 documented as deliberate conservatism; and, as a narrower option, honouring quotes only while leaving the substitution and background-& holes open. because Quote-unawareness was never conservatism — a && or newline inside a quoted string is not a separator, so reading it as one is simply wrong, and it happened to fail toward logging by accident rather than design. The cost was concrete: this repo's own multi-line commit messages defeated the exemption, so the record could not settle and every session opened with a false staleness warning. The two extra holes are the same defect in the other direction — `git log $(rm -rf x)` rode the leading git to an exemption, swallowing real work — and closing them in the same scan is what makes "ambiguity resolves toward logging" true as stated instead of accidental.
